checks.expected:
# First development baseline experiment, v1

Owner: chief. Specified before any strategy outcomes. Independent review and accepted
core implementation are required before experiment dispatch. Fixed parameters:
specs/development_baselines_v1.json. This is a development design, not the final
freeze or a customer recommendation.

## Question and scope

Measure the required equal-weight annual baseline against two simple references:
keep initial bills, and initially buy equal weights then preserve holdings. This
isolates costs and weight drift from annual rebalancing. Buy-and-hold does not
estimate trade benefit and cannot alone satisfy the full Balanced requirement.

Use only original synthetic scenarios 1--120. Each independently starts with wealth
100 in bills. No fitted parameter, forecast, optimizer, random search, daily
conversion, withdrawal, extra fee or terminal liquidation. Audited scenario
outcomes are valid competition evidence; they are not historical forecasts.

This pilot does not assign Conservative/Balanced/Growth targets, decide suitability
or conclude whether automatic target updates add value. Those require later
development design, a cost-aware rule and profile analysis.

## Actions and timing

Asset order: equity, bond, bill proxy. bills_keep keeps dollar holdings at every
review. equal_weight_annual requests exact thirds every review, including period 1.
equal_weight_buy_hold requests thirds in period 1 and keeps holdings thereafter.
All three have one review each year. Keep costs zero.

Construct and record each action using policy ID, year, pre-return holdings and
available history before obtaining that year's returns or inflation. Use the locked
transfer and pro-rata fee convention, then returns, then exact CPI deflation.

Actions do not depend on horizon. Prefixes of one 30-year ledger per policy/scenario
therefore support H=5,6,15,25,30. Exclude all wealth, fees and reviews after H from
H-year metrics; independently verify prefix reruns. Common policy comparison: H=30.
Profile A/B/C/D/E uses H=5/15/30/25/6. Tolerances are not guaranteed bounds.

## Metrics and aggregation

Apply specs/ACCOUNTING.md: real CAGR; sample standard deviation of annual net real
wealth returns (ddof=1); maximum real drawdown including initial, post-fee and
year-end observations. Calculate scenario metrics before scenario aggregation.

For each policy/horizon report median and p10 growth, median and p90 loss, median
annual fluctuation, median terminal real wealth, median cumulative nominal fees,
and trade percentages including/excluding the initial review. Use linear quantiles.
Growth and fluctuation are percentage points per year; loss and trade share are
percent; wealth and nominal fee sums use initial nominal units, with real wealth
in time-zero purchasing power. Nominal fee sums are descriptive, not real welfare
losses. Summary trade shares use pooled trade counts / pooled review counts:
120*H or 120*(H-1); scenario denominators are H or H-1. Trade means transfer >1e-10.

Severe case: greatest large loss within each policy/horizon; exact ties choose
smallest scenario ID. Report ID, growth, loss, real terminal wealth, drawdown
peak/trough locations (year and initial/post_fee/end kind), and both trade shares.
This finite-sample maximum is not a probabilistic bound.

For each alternative minus equal_weight_annual on the same scenario/horizon,
record paired differences in growth, loss, terminal real wealth, nominal fee sum,
and both trade shares. Positive loss difference means worse. These are descriptive
comparisons with no significance claim or winner-selection threshold.

## Outputs in the future fixed run directory

The future HY3 task will specify an already-pushed source SHA and output directory.

- run_manifest.json: schema/plan ID; source SHA; config/code/input hashes; command;
  Python/package versions; UTC start/end; split and parameters; CPU runtime;
  completed/failed status; hashes of every other output file.
- annual_ledgers.csv: 10,800 rows keyed by policy/scenario/year. Record action,
  pre-trade holdings/wealth, target when applicable, transfer, fee, post-fee
  holdings/wealth, annual returns, inflation, end holdings/wealth, CPI before/after,
  post-fee/end real wealth. Asset components have separate numeric columns.
- scenario_metrics.csv: 1,800 policy/scenario/horizon rows; all defined metrics,
  fee sums, trade counts, review denominators, percentages, split and units.
- summary.csv: 15 policy/horizon rows with the specified aggregates and severe
  case, scenario count 120, horizon, split and metric unit columns.
- paired_differences.csv: 1,200 alternative/scenario/horizon rows with unit columns.
- checks.json: checks actually run, counts, failures and maximum numerical residuals.

CSV: UTF-8, deterministic order, round-trip float precision. Metrics must be finite.
Keep targets may be blank; all monetary zeros are explicit. No H=1 metrics here.

## Acceptance and next handoff

First accept chief's independent review of SOL-001, HY3-001 source/split evidence,
and Sol's independent review of this design. Then publish and review the actual
pilot driver before assigning HY3 fixed commands. HY3 must not invent a missing
driver or infer an API. No task can reference unpushed source.

Required checks:

1. Development hash, schema, complete unique IDs/periods and row counts. Performance
   driver reads neither raw nor final data.
2. Independent toy oracle: 20-unit transfer, initial fee, exact keep, two-year
   path, inflation-only loss and initial-fee drawdown followed by recovery.
3. Every ledger: nonnegative finite holdings, budget balance, fee before returns,
   keep preservation, exact CPI, baseline target. Toy abs=1e-9; ledger rel=1e-10.
4. All policies, horizons, scenarios and required files/counts/hashes.
5. IDs 1,60,120: independently rerun all prefixes and recompute metrics from
   holdings. Perturb returns/inflation at and after year 10; actions through year
   10 and earlier states stay unchanged. Single-scenario and batch outputs agree.
6. A later separate Sol task recomputes representative HY3 ledgers, quantiles,
   paired differences and severe-case selections.

Preserve every failure and candidate. Validation tier: scenario-check.
After audit, pilot supports descriptive baseline comparisons. Recommendations need
later suitability, cost-aware policy development and sensitivity. All later tuning
uses development evidence. Final 121--180 stays closed until a separate freeze.

checks.expected:
"""Chief's rational oracle, authored before reviewing Sol's implementation.
No production imports or scenario files. These are toy checks, not performance.
"""
import argparse
from fractions import Fraction as F
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

def exact(x):
    return {"rational": str(x), "value": float(x)}

def build():
    k = F(1, 400)
    transfer, fee = F(20), F(20)*k
    assert fee == F(1, 20)
    allocated = [(100-fee)*F(1, 5), F(0), (100-fee)*F(4, 5)]
    assert allocated == [F(1999, 100), F(0), F(1999, 25)]
    # Explicit scalar algebra, not an imported production rebalance function.
    fee1 = F(200, 3)*k
    holding1 = (100-fee1)/3
    end1 = [holding1*F(11, 10), holding1, holding1*F(19, 20)]
    wealth1 = sum(end1)
    # Only equity exceeds the new one-third target.
    transfer2 = end1[0]-wealth1/3
    assert transfer2 == sum(abs(wealth1/3-x) for x in end1)/2
    fee2 = transfer2*k
    holding2 = (wealth1-fee2)/3
    end2 = [holding2*F(4, 5), holding2*F(11, 10), holding2]
    cpi = F(51, 50)
    real1, real_trade2, real2 = wealth1/cpi, (wealth1-fee2)/cpi, sum(end2)/cpi
    path = [F(100), 100-fee1, real1, real_trade2, real2]
    peak, drawdown = F(100), F(0)
    for value in path:
        peak = max(peak, value)
        drawdown = max(drawdown, 1-value/peak)
    returns = [real1/100-1, real2/real1-1]
    mean_return = sum(returns)/2
    variance = sum((x-mean_return)**2 for x in returns)  # H-1 = 1
    assert sum(end1) == (100-fee1)*F(61, 60)
    assert sum(end2) == (wealth1-fee2)*F(29, 30)
    assert drawdown == 1-real2/100
    recovery_terminal = (100-fee1)*F(11, 10)
    assert recovery_terminal > 100
    return {
        "schema_version": 1, "author_role": "chief",
        "purpose": "Independent toy oracle; no scenario outcomes or production imports",
        "fee_rate": exact(k),
        "twenty_unit_transfer": {
            "pre_holdings": [0, 0, 100], "target": ["1/5", "0", "4/5"],
            "transfer": exact(transfer), "fee": exact(fee),
            "post_fee_holdings": [exact(x) for x in allocated]},
        "all_equity_initial": {
            "transfer": exact(F(100)), "fee": exact(F(1, 4)),
            "post_fee_wealth": exact(F(399, 4))},
        "keep_bills_inflation_only": {
            "inflation": exact(F(1, 10)), "fee": exact(F(0)),
            "real_terminal": exact(F(1000, 11)),
            "growth_pct_pa": exact(-F(100, 11)),
            "max_real_drawdown_pct": exact(F(100, 11)),
            "volatility_pct_pa": None,
            "volatility_note": "Undefined at H=1; do not substitute zero."},
        "initial_fee_then_recovery": {
            "returns": ["1/10", "1/10", "1/10"], "inflation": "0",
            "real_post_fee": exact(100-fee1), "real_terminal": exact(recovery_terminal),
            "max_real_drawdown_pct": exact(F(1, 6))},
        "equal_weight_two_year": {
            "returns": [["1/10", "0", "-1/20"], ["-1/5", "1/10", "0"]],
            "inflation": ["1/50", "0"], "initial_holdings": [0, 0, 100],
            "transfer": [exact(F(200, 3)), exact(transfer2)],
            "fees": [exact(fee1), exact(fee2)],
            "post_fee_each_holding": [exact(holding1), exact(holding2)],
            "end_holdings": [[exact(x) for x in end1], [exact(x) for x in end2]],
            "real_path_initial_trade_end_trade_end": [exact(x) for x in path],
            "annual_net_real_returns": [exact(x) for x in returns],
            "terminal_real_wealth": exact(real2),
            "growth_pct_pa": 100*(math.sqrt(float(real2/100))-1),
            "volatility_pct_pa_ddof1": 100*math.sqrt(float(variance)),
            "max_real_drawdown_pct": exact(100*drawdown),
            "trade_share_including_initial_pct": 100,
            "trade_share_excluding_initial_pct": 100},
        "quantile_linear_fixture": {
            "values": [0, 10, 20, 30], "p10": 3, "median": 15, "p90": 27},
        "comparison_tolerance": {"absolute_toy": 1e-9, "relative_ledger": 1e-10}
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--check", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    report = build()
    if args.check:
        assert json.loads(args.check.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == report
        print("Rational oracle snapshot matches all independently derived fixtures.")
    if args.output:
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2)+"\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if not args.output and not args.check:
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))

# Authoritative task lock — 2026-10-19

Source: `problem/2026_MCM_SafeInvest.pdf` (3 pages). This file summarizes the competition requirements, not additional instructions from the source document.

## Deliverables

1. Define Conservative, Balanced and Growth allocations/rules; separate ordinary fluctuations from unusually large losses; use purchasing power. An explainable suitability process must consider horizon, temporary loss tolerance and liquidity, and may request human review. Profiles: A=(5,10%,high), B=(15,25%,medium), C=(30,40%,low), D=(25,15%,medium), E=(6,35%,high). The loss tolerance is not a guarantee. Evaluate each profile using its own horizon.
2. Balanced policy chooses keep, rebalance, target change or human review. Trade only for an estimated benefit that justifies cost, using information available before that period. Compare to a fixed one-third/one-third/one-third target restored every review. Report scenario median growth, median large loss, p10 growth, p90 large loss, a severe-loss case and percentage of reviews involving trades. Decide honestly whether automatic target updates add value. One customer explanation <=50 English words.
3. Test one important assumption or transaction-cost rate, explain any change to the recommendation, state limitations and a trigger for review/suspension, and specify holdings/actions while review is pending.

## Inputs and nonnegotiable conditions

- 180 independent synthetic scenarios, 30 annual observations each; six original CSV fields. Never concatenate independent scenarios into a historical time series.
- Development and tuning: scenario IDs 1–120. Final evaluation: IDs 121–180, after strategy/parameters/metrics/severe-case selection are frozen. Metadata validation of the complete file is permitted; final outcomes are not development evidence.
- Starting nominal wealth 100 entirely in bills. No deposits/withdrawals. Long-only, fully invested in three assets, including bills. No borrowing or terminal liquidation fee.
- A period-t decision may use only that scenario's observations through t−1; development-calibrated parameters are permitted. Internal development validation must fit on its training scenarios only.
- Cost=0.0025 times money moved between assets, each transfer counted once. A 20-unit transfer costs 0.05. Include initial allocation; deduct fee before period returns.
- Real return=(1+nominal return)/(1+inflation)−1. Bills are not guaranteed safe in real terms.

## Reporting and deadline

English report <=10 A4 pages, font >=11pt, all three member names and an AI-use disclosure. Source code supplement ZIP <=50MB. Deadline: 2026-10-20 23:59 Asia/Shanghai. Final submission is by the human team leader.

## Initial research route, not a finding

Begin with exact accounting, the required equal-weight baseline, static allocation candidates and a cost-aware no-trade policy. Add automatic target changes only if development evidence supports their added complexity. Use simple transparent rules and scenario-based risk measures before considering stochastic optimization. Freeze experiment selection rules before opening final outcomes.

checks.expected:
# Accounting and metric contract v1

This fixes a disclosed modeling convention where the problem leaves fee payment details unspecified. Sol must review this convention before reporting a correct implementation; disagreements go to the coordinator rather than silent changes.

Let pre-trade holdings h>=0, W=sum(h), current weights u=h/W, and desired target w>=0 with sum(w)=1. For a target rebalance, measure the intended transfer on pre-fee wealth: T=(W/2)*sum(abs(w-u)), c=k*T. Charge c before returns and allocate remaining wealth proportionally to target: h_plus=(W-c)*w. This is a pre-fee transfer convention with pro-rata fee funding. The tiny fee-funding adjustment is not charged again. It keeps the target exact after fees and avoids double counting. Record intended transferred amount, fee, post-fee holdings and wealth explicitly.

Examples at k=0.0025 and h=(0,0,100):
- Keep bills: T=0, c=0, W_plus=100.
- Target (0.2,0,0.8): T=20, c=0.05, h_plus=(19.99,0,79.96).
- Equal weight: T=200/3, c=1/6, W_plus=599/6; each holding=599/18.
- All equity: T=100, c=0.25, h_plus=(99.75,0,0).

If action=keep, preserve dollar holdings exactly and charge zero. The equal-weight baseline requests target (1/3,1/3,1/3) in every period including period 1. Even a review can produce T=0 if holdings already match.

Then h_end,i=h_plus,i*(1+r_t,i). CPI_t=CPI_(t−1)*(1+inflation_t), CPI_0=1. Real wealth at trade is sum(h_plus)/CPI_(t−1), at year end=sum(h_end)/CPI_t. A decision object must be created before accessing r_t or inflation_t.

For horizon H, growth=100*((real_W_H/100)^(1/H)−1), in percentage points per year. Ordinary fluctuation=sample standard deviation of annual net real wealth returns in percentage points (ddof=1; H>=2). Large loss=100*max_t(1−real_W_t/running_peak), including initial wealth and both post-fee and year-end wealth observations. Larger means worse; minimum zero. Quantiles across independent scenarios use linear interpolation. Never confuse p90 loss with a guaranteed bound or CVaR.

Trade share=100*number(T>1e−10)/number(review periods), including the initial review; additionally report the share excluding initial allocation. Every result records horizon, units and split. Profile horizons are 5,15,30,25,6 respectively. Initial policy comparison uses the common 30-year market horizon; report this explicitly.

Mandatory invariants: nonnegative finite holdings, fully invested after fees, W=W_plus+c, no fee on keep, fees precede returns, exact compounded inflation, initial wealth in drawdown peak, and future-data perturbations leave earlier decisions unchanged. Solver tolerance must be documented; accounting comparisons use abs tolerance 1e−9 on toy fixtures and relative tolerance 1e−10 on ordinary-sized ledgers.

checks.expected:
# Three-computer protocol v1

## Roles

| Role | Model/client | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chief | GPT-6 Astra xhigh / coordinator Codex | Mathematical decisions, clear task specifications, policy design, integration, evidence selection, final English paper |
| sol | GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh / remote Codex | Accounting/backtest implementation, targeted tests, independent review of chief's policy and HY3's experiments |
| hy3 | HY3 / remote WorkBuddy | Supervise deterministic Python worker, run specified experiments, preserve ledgers and checks, diagnose/report execution failures |

This is a responsibility allocation, not a measured claim about HY3's relative intelligence. Numeric work is done by Python, not model mental arithmetic. Computational volume is tiny (three assets, 5,400 annual observations); all nodes can use CPU. GPU on chief is optional.

## Branches and directories

- `main`: accepted code/specifications/results/report plus coordinator-owned dispatch queue.
- `archive/pre-coordination-20261019`: historical setup before this protocol.
- `work/sol/<task>-a<attempt>` and `work/hy3/<task>-a<attempt>`: one immutable task attempt each; completion receipt is `handoff/<task>/result.json`.
- `status/chief`, `status/sol`, `status/hy3`: lightweight machine status with single-writer leases. These branches contain only `status.json` and are never merged into main.

| Directory | Purpose / authority |
| --- | --- |
| `problem/`, `data/raw/` | Original source files, no worker edits |
| `data/development/` | Scenarios 1–120 |
| `data/final_holdout/` | Scenarios 121–180, final gate required |
| `specs/` | Coordinator's mathematical and experimental contracts |
| `src/safeinvest/`, `tests/` | Implementations and meaningful checks; modified only by assigned tasks |
| `results/development/`, `results/final/` | Machine-readable results with run provenance |
| `audit/` | Independent numerical review and findings |
| `report/` | Final manuscript, figures and evidence-to-claim mapping |
| `ops/tasks/`, `ops/queue.json` | Coordinator dispatches immutable tasks and records acceptance |
| `ops/prompts/` | Forwardable onboarding and coordinator continuation |
| `scripts/` | Common tools; coordinator-maintained |
| `handoff/` | Task result manifests, evidence and diagnosis |
| `.runtime/`, `.venv/` | Ignored local state, logs, worktrees, credentials-free settings and environment |

## Task state and ownership

`waiting -> ready -> worker running -> submitted completed/failed -> coordinator accepted or new attempt`.

Queue state is coordinator-owned: `waiting`, `ready`, `accepted`, `cancelled`. Worker execution states live in status/result manifests, not in a shared mutable queue. Owner is explicit; workers cannot steal work. A local exclusive PID lock plus a remote ten-minute role lease prevents accidental duplicate workers. If a machine crashes, inspect the lock PID before removing a stale local lock; a different machine waits for lease expiry or obtains an explicit handover.

An immutable task has id, attempt, owner, 40-character base_commit, kind, dependencies, instructions, permitted paths, deliverables, explicit commands/checks and timeout. Do not edit a published attempt. A changed task needs an incremented attempt (and new branch); a different objective needs a new id. Queue statuses may change without changing task contents.

The runner uses a separate worktree at the pinned base. It does not merge arbitrary current main into an in-flight experiment. It checks the changed paths, tests and required output files before committing and pushing. No force push is used. The input/source version remains traceable even if main advances while a computation runs.

## Acceptance and self-checks

1. Structural checks: task identity/hash, branch, source commit, permitted paths and required outputs.
2. Deterministic checks: expected fixtures, accounting identities, inflation, weights, no-lookahead perturbation, split guards and input hashes.
3. Independent review: chief reviews Sol implementation; Sol independently recomputes selected chief/HY3 outputs. A model writing both code and tests is not independent validation.
4. Result promotion: chief inspects the exact result commit and actual reports, resolves any required review, integrates only accepted changes, and records the reviewed SHA in the queue. A worker's word “completed” is not enough.
5. Research checks: record every candidate, use only development outcomes to tune, freeze policy/metrics/parameters/selection rules, then final evaluation once with no further tuning. Final bug corrections remain disclosed and do not erase contamination history.

`ops/freeze.json` must bind code SHA, parameters, metrics, severe-case rule and input hashes. A final task supplies SHA256 of its canonical UTF-8 contents (strip outer whitespace, matching the runner's `git show` read), and `ops/control.json.final_data_open` must be true. This is a procedural study gate, not protection against collaborators deliberately opening a tracked file.

## Start the two remote machines

Forward `ops/prompts/START_SOL.txt` or `START_HY3.txt`. Each machine clones this repo, logs in to GitHub with its own account, and has collaborator write access. Git pushes must work without a recurring login dialog before starting a background runner. Do not share credentials.

Create a local Python 3.12 virtual environment and install `requirements.txt` for numeric jobs. Metadata validation and the runner itself need only standard Python. Commands below assume `python` is the selected interpreter:

```text
python scripts/coop.py doctor --role sol
python scripts/coop.py watch --role sol --backend codex
```

For WorkBuddy's machine:

```text
python scripts/coop.py doctor --role hy3
python scripts/coop.py watch --role hy3 --backend commands
```

The HY3 worker is intentionally deterministic: it runs the coordinator's commands. WorkBuddy handles setup and failure explanation. A local WorkBuddy scheduled task can periodically check its `.runtime/hy3-status.json` / `hy3-error.json` and report only a meaningful change; it must not start duplicate workers. Use the actual WorkBuddy scheduler, not an assumed CodeBuddy CLI. Do not use cloud scheduling for files that exist only on this local machine.

Run `python scripts/coop.py once --role ... --backend ...` for a single cycle. `python scripts/coop.py status` reads all machine states. `python scripts/coop.py stop` writes a local STOP file. To resume, inspect unfinished work and remove only that known STOP file, then restart. Do not delete `.runtime/` wholesale: it can contain unfinished task worktrees.

For unattended Windows use, launch the command with a hidden background process and redirect logs to `.runtime/`; keep the computer awake and network connected. On macOS/Linux use the platform's process manager. Login prompts, sleeping computers, model quotas and denied permissions can stop progress; report actual process and remote status rather than claiming “always running.”

## Coordinator loop

`python scripts/coop.py watch --role chief --backend codex` watches task-branch changes and worker registration/error changes. Its first pass records the initial state so it does not duplicate bootstrap work. Meaningful changes invoke GPT-6 Astra xhigh with `CHIEF_TICK.txt`; idle heartbeat changes do not invoke the model. Chief serializes integration and dispatch, then pushes main. The runner stops after two consecutive infrastructure failures, local STOP, project stop state or the configured deadline. A failed task is not automatically rerun; chief creates a corrected attempt.

There is no automatic wakeup of this exact original chat from a background process. During an active chat, the coordinator reports needs here; background work records needs in status/error files and GitHub, and the remote clients can surface them using their own notification mechanisms. Avoid claiming an unattended process can send a chat message unless that integration has actually been configured.

## Research stages

1. Bootstrap, environment registration and data validation.
2. Sol implements and challenges the accounting/baseline contract; chief independently checks fixtures and locks metrics.
3. Chief specifies static candidates, suitability and conservative cost-aware policy; HY3 runs explicit development experiments.
4. Sol independently audits no-lookahead, costs, metrics and representative ledgers; chief chooses the simplest supported strategy and issues sensitivity jobs.
5. Freeze the exact final protocol. HY3 runs one specified final evaluation. Sol verifies evidence and chief decides recommendations without tuning to final outcomes.
6. Chief writes/integrates the English <=10-page report and <=50MB code supplement. Sol checks evidence and mathematical statements; HY3 regenerates specified final tables/figures. Humans supply member names and submit.

## References for execution adapters

- Codex supports scripted `exec`, structured results and saved CLI login: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode
- WorkBuddy supports local scheduled tasks and model/workspace selection: https://www.workbuddy.cn/docs/workbuddy/From-Beginner-to-Expert-Guide/Function-Description/Automation-Guide
- Model assignment rationale: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-selection

## Task state and ownership

`waiting -> ready -> worker running -> submitted completed/failed -> coordinator accepted or new attempt`.

Queue state is coordinator-owned: `waiting`, `ready`, `accepted`, `cancelled`. Worker execution states live in status/result manifests, not in a shared mutable queue. Owner is explicit; workers cannot steal work. A local exclusive PID lock plus a remote ten-minute role lease prevents accidental duplicate workers. If a machine crashes, inspect the lock PID before removing a stale local lock; a different machine waits for lease expiry or obtains an explicit handover.

An immutable task has id, attempt, owner, 40-character base_commit, kind, dependencies, instructions, permitted paths, deliverables, explicit commands/checks and timeout. Do not edit a published attempt. A changed task needs an incremented attempt (and new branch); a different objective needs a new id. Queue statuses may change without changing task contents.

The runner uses a separate worktree at the pinned base. It does not merge arbitrary current main into an in-flight experiment. It checks the changed paths, tests and required output files before committing and pushing. No force push is used. The input/source version remains traceable even if main advances while a computation runs.

## Acceptance and self-checks

1. Structural checks: task identity/hash, branch, source commit, permitted paths and required outputs.
2. Deterministic checks: expected fixtures, accounting identities, inflation, weights, no-lookahead perturbation, split guards and input hashes.
3. Independent review: chief reviews Sol implementation; Sol independently recomputes selected chief/HY3 outputs. A model writing both code and tests is not independent validation.
4. Result promotion: chief inspects the exact result commit and actual reports, resolves any required review, integrates only accepted changes, and records the reviewed SHA in the queue. A worker's word “completed” is not enough.
5. Research checks: record every candidate, use only development outcomes to tune, freeze policy/metrics/parameters/selection rules, then final evaluation once with no further tuning. Final bug corrections remain disclosed and do not erase contamination history.

`ops/freeze.json` must bind code SHA, parameters, metrics, severe-case rule and input hashes. A final task supplies SHA256 of its canonical UTF-8 contents (strip outer whitespace, matching the runner's `git show` read), and `ops/control.json.final_data_open` must be true. This is a procedural study gate, not protection against collaborators deliberately opening a tracked file.

## Start the two remote machines

Forward `ops/prompts/START_SOL.txt` or `START_HY3.txt`. Each machine clones this repo, logs in to GitHub with its own account, and has collaborator write access. Git pushes must work without a recurring login dialog before starting a background runner. Do not share credentials.

Create a local Python 3.12 virtual environment and install `requirements.txt` for numeric jobs. Metadata validation and the runner itself need only standard Python. Commands below assume `python` is the selected interpreter:

```text
python scripts/coop.py doctor --role sol
python scripts/coop.py watch --role sol --backend codex
```

For WorkBuddy's machine:

```text
python scripts/coop.py doctor --role hy3
python scripts/coop.py watch --role hy3 --backend commands
```

The HY3 worker is intentionally deterministic: it runs the coordinator's commands. WorkBuddy handles setup and failure explanation. A local WorkBuddy scheduled task can periodically check its `.runtime/hy3-status.json` / `hy3-error.json` and report only a meaningful change; it must not start duplicate workers. Use the actual WorkBuddy scheduler, not an assumed CodeBuddy CLI. Do not use cloud scheduling for files that exist only on this local machine.

Run `python scripts/coop.py once --role ... --backend ...` for a single cycle. `python scripts/coop.py status` reads all machine states. `python scripts/coop.py stop` writes a local STOP file. To resume, inspect unfinished work and remove only that known STOP file, then restart. Do not delete `.runtime/` wholesale: it can contain unfinished task worktrees.

For unattended Windows use, launch the command with a hidden background process and redirect logs to `.runtime/`; keep the computer awake and network connected. On macOS/Linux use the platform's process manager. Login prompts, sleeping computers, model quotas and denied permissions can stop progress; report actual process and remote status rather than claiming “always running.”

## Coordinator loop

`python scripts/coop.py watch --role chief --backend codex` watches task-branch changes and worker registration/error changes. Its first pass records the initial state so it does not duplicate bootstrap work. Meaningful changes invoke GPT-6 Astra xhigh with `CHIEF_TICK.txt`; idle heartbeat changes do not invoke the model. Chief serializes integration and dispatch, then pushes main. The runner stops after two consecutive infrastructure failures, local STOP, project stop state or the configured deadline. A failed task is not automatically rerun; chief creates a corrected attempt.

There is no automatic wakeup of this exact original chat from a background process. During an active chat, the coordinator reports needs here; background work records needs in status/error files and GitHub, and the remote clients can surface them using their own notification mechanisms. Avoid claiming an unattended process can send a chat message unless that integration has actually been configured.

## Research stages

1. Bootstrap, environment registration and data validation.
2. Sol implements and challenges the accounting/baseline contract; chief independently checks fixtures and locks metrics.
3. Chief specifies static candidates, suitability and conservative cost-aware policy; HY3 runs explicit development experiments.
4. Sol independently audits no-lookahead, costs, metrics and representative ledgers; chief chooses the simplest supported strategy and issues sensitivity jobs.
5. Freeze the exact final protocol. HY3 runs one specified final evaluation. Sol verifies evidence and chief decides recommendations without tuning to final outcomes.
6. Chief writes/integrates the English <=10-page report and <=50MB code supplement. Sol checks evidence and mathematical statements; HY3 regenerates specified final tables/figures. Humans supply member names and submit.
